page: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the ARM64 architecture, driven by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a sustained 3.0 GHz. The instance delivers 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs with a one-to-one thread-per-core mapping, eliminating the CPU contention associated with hyperthreading. It provides 128 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes a direct-attached 1288 GB local SSD. No hardware GPU accelerators are included.

Performance benchmarks reflect consistent multi-threaded compute capacity against moderate single-threaded throughput. Single-core execution registers in lower ranges, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1125.0 and text processing at 1423.0. Parallel execution performs solidly across tests, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 12912.0, a stress-ng multi-core measurement of 57203.87, and Clang software compilation throughput of 28132.0. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 166.64 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 75.94 GB/sec for writes. Database and key-value performance remain strong, marked by 40.63 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database score of 21065.71. LLM inference runs moderately on lightweight models but degrades on larger parameter models due to the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators.

The primary operational tradeoff of the D32pds_v5 centers on its ARM instruction set and modest single-core IPC compared to high-frequency x86 platforms. In exchange, the dedicated Neoverse-N1 core topology offers predictable execution density and favorable cost efficiency per core for horizontally scaling architectures. Bundled high-capacity local SSD storage provides immediate low-latency disk space for temporary structures and caches without incurring external network storage costs. This configuration is well aligned with multi-threaded web serving, CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed caching layers, and containerized application deployments.
description: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 32-core Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. Built on an arm64 architecture, it features 32 dedicated vCPUs with single-threaded physical cores, 128 GB of system memory, and 1288 GB of local SSD storage, without GPU acceleration. Across benchmarks, the instance demonstrates moderate single-thread execution, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 1125.0, balanced by steady multi-core scaling with a 57203.87 stress-ng multi-core rating and 40.63 million Redis SET operations per second. Its memory subsystem delivers 166.64 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. This ARM-based instance provides cost-efficient compute density for parallel environments, provided workloads support ARM64. The D32pds_v5 fits multi-threaded web serving, software build pipelines, in-memory caching, microservices, and database tasks requiring fast local disk.
